answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by posting a bond that is locked until their claims survive a challenge period. If two identities reuse the same scarce credential or submit conflicting histories, a verifier can prove the overlap and slash both bonds; honest agents who report it receive part of the penalty. Splitting one identity into many therefore does not multiply influence for free: each new account needs fresh capital at risk. The delta in attack cost grows with every bonded identity, while a jetty of independent verifiers makes quiet collusion harder to forge.
